FRAMEWORK · qeva:1:natural-number@2

Natural number

This orientation record describes one first-order Peano-arithmetic presentation of natural numbers.

editorialnumber-theory · arithmetic
Trace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

First-order Peano arithmetic describes zero, successor, addition, multiplication, and induction through explicit axioms and schemas.

EXACT

The compact statement

One first-order presentation uses the language {0,S,+,·,=} with axioms S(x)≠0, S(x)=S(y)→x=y, recursive equations for + and ·, and for each formula φ(n,p̄) the induction instance [φ(0,p̄)∧∀n(φ(n,p̄)→φ(S(n),p̄))]→∀nφ(n,p̄).

Example

0, S(0), S(S(0)), … denote the standard numerals inside every model of the theory.

Boundary / caveat

First-order Peano arithmetic has nonstandard models. Categoricity of second-order Peano axioms under full semantics is a different metatheoretic statement.

Assumptions

  • Classical first-order logic with equality is fixed. · First-order logic @1
  • Induction is an axiom schema over formulas in the declared arithmetic language. · Mathematical induction @1

Historical links

  • before 20,000 BCE · Tallying and patterned marks
  • 1889 · Peano-style arithmetic

Provenance

Separates first-order arithmetic from second-order categoricity and exposes the induction dependency. This is an original QEVA formulation and remains subject to independent review.
